New machine. Its objects are: temulor, fudoti, lamesen, pidofik, maleres, timinir.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects together to see how the machine responds.

TEST: temulor, fudoti, lamesen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up. Testing the other three next shows how the nexioms are split: if this group also lights, there is probably one nexiom in each half.

TEST: pidofik, maleres, timinir
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up and the second did not. Under the simplest rules (lights if any nexiom is present, or only if both are), both nexioms must be among temulor, fudoti and lamesen. Testing temulor alone checks whether it is a nexiom, and also hints at which kind of rule this machine follows.

TEST: temulor
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Since the first group lit up and the second did not, the nexioms cannot be in pidofik, maleres or timinir. That leaves temulor, fudoti and lamesen.

- **If the machine lights when any nexiom is present:** temulor alone not lighting rules it out. The pair would have to be fudoti and lamesen.
- **If the machine lights only when both nexioms are present:** temulor alone would never light. The pair could be any two of temulor, fudoti and lamesen.

So fudoti and lamesen is the only pair that fits both rules, which makes it the most likely answer. Testing exactly those two settles it if the machine lights. If it does not light, the pair must include temulor, and I'll have to guess between temulor with fudoti and temulor with lamesen.

TEST: fudoti, lamesen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The four results:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| temulor, fudoti, lamesen | lit up |
| pidofik, maleres, timinir | did not light |
| temulor | did not light |
| fudoti, lamesen | did not light |

**Ruling out "lights if any nexiom is present":** temulor alone did not light, so temulor would not be a nexiom. Fudoti and lamesen together did not light, so neither of them would be one either. But then the first group, which lit up, would have no nexiom. So this rule cannot be right.

**"Lights only when both nexioms are present" fits all four results:**
- The first group lit, so both nexioms are among temulor, fudoti and lamesen.
- The second group stays dark because it has no nexioms.
- Temulor alone stays dark because one nexiom is not enough.
- Fudoti and lamesen did not light, so they are not the pair. That means temulor is one of the nexioms.

That leaves two equally possible answers: temulor with fudoti, or temulor with lamesen. My tests cannot tell them apart, so this is a 50/50 guess. I'm picking temulor with fudoti.

ANSWER: nexioms = temulor, fudoti
One last question. If only fudoti were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. The only rule that fits all four results is that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Fudoti alone is at most one nexiom, so it would not light. This holds whether or not fudoti is actually a nexiom, so it doesn't depend on my 50/50 guess.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: gunasi, mufito, fedago, biragus, rapapik, bezusin.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by splitting the six objects into two halves of three, as planned in my notes. This test gives useful information under either an AND or an OR rule.

TEST: gunasi, mufito, fedago
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Gunasi, mufito and fedago did not light the machine. Under an OR rule, that means both nexioms are among biragus, rapapik and bezusin. Under an AND rule, it only means the two nexioms are not both in the first half. Testing the other half next separates these cases: if it lights, the pair is in that half.

TEST: biragus, rapapik, bezusin
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit, which rules out an OR rule: under OR, whichever half held a nexiom would have lit. Under an AND rule, this means the nexioms are split, one in {gunasi, mufito, fedago} and one in {biragus, rapapik, bezusin}. That leaves 9 possible pairs. Two yes/no tests can only separate 4 groups, so I can't guarantee the answer. I'll split the candidates as evenly as I can. This test lights only if the pair is (gunasi or mufito) with (biragus or rapapik), which covers 4 of the 9 pairs.

TEST: gunasi, mufito, biragus, rapapik
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine lit when gunasi, mufito, biragus and rapapik were on together. Neither half lit alone, so the rule appears to be AND. Under AND, the pair must be one of {gunasi, mufito} together with one of {biragus, rapapik}, which leaves 4 possible pairs. One test can't separate 4 pairs, so whatever I test, my final chance of naming the right pair is 1 in 2.

I'll test the single pair gunasi + biragus. If it lights, that is the answer for certain. If not, I'll have to guess among the other three pairs.

TEST: gunasi, biragus
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The pair gunasi + biragus did not light, so it is ruled out. Assuming the rule is AND, three pairs remain:

- gunasi + rapapik
- mufito + biragus
- mufito + rapapik

Nothing favours one of these over the others, so this is a 1-in-3 guess. Testing a single pair gave an overall 1-in-2 chance, but only because it might have lit and confirmed the answer. Now that it didn't, the odds are worse.

Note for future machines: when neither 3/3 half lights, the pair is split across the halves. That leaves 9 possible pairs, and three tests can't reliably find the answer. Next time, I should consider a first split that leaves fewer cases afterward.

ANSWER: nexioms = mufito, rapapik
One last question. If only mufito were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Most likely no. My working assumption is an AND rule: the machine lights only when both nexioms are on together. That fits all four results.

- Neither half lit, which rules out OR.
- Gunasi, mufito, biragus and rapapik together lit.
- Gunasi and biragus together did not light.

Under AND, one object alone never lights, even if it is a nexiom. So mufito alone should not light the machine.

I can't be certain, though. An "exactly one nexiom" rule also fits all four results if the nexioms are fedago and mufito, and under that rule mufito alone would light. I never tested a single object, so I can't rule this out. I'm going with AND because it is the simpler rule and matches what I saw on the last machine.

PROBE: no

I won't assume that, but I'll start with a test that splits the AND case well. If I place four objects, AND lights for 6 of the 15 pairs and stays dark for 9. That is close to an even split.

TEST: sufilo, lesezin, lopazok, vokima
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

After the dark first test, the remaining pairs depend on the rule:
- **AND:** 9 pairs are still possible, namely any pair that includes relegel or vepalu.
- **OR:** only relegel + vepalu is left.
- **XOR (exactly one nexiom lights it):** 7 pairs remain. These are the 6 pairs inside the first group plus relegel + vepalu.

For the next test I'll place relegel, vepalu, sufilo and lesezin.
- **Under AND:** it lights for 5 of the 9 pairs (relegel+vepalu, relegel+sufilo, relegel+lesezin, vepalu+sufilo, vepalu+lesezin). That is close to an even split.

- **OR rule:** relegel+vepalu.

That is the most even split I can get.

Five pairs still fit all three results:
- **AND:** relegel+vepalu, relegel+sufilo or vepalu+sufilo.
- **OR:** relegel+vepalu.
- **XOR:** sufilo+lopazok or sufilo+vokima.

One test cannot separate five pairs, so I'll favour AND, which both earlier machines used. Placing relegel and sufilo together gives these outcomes:
- **If it lights:** relegel+sufilo is the most likely answer under AND. The OR pair relegel+vepalu or either XOR pair would also light it.
- **If it stays dark:** only relegel+vepalu or vepalu+sufilo is left, both under AND.

TEST: relegel, sufilo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Every pair left includes vepalu, but I can't tell which object is its partner.

**What the last dark result rules out:**
- **OR:** relegel+vepalu is ruled out, because relegel alone would have lit it.
- **XOR:** sufilo+lopazok and sufilo+vokima are ruled out, because sufilo alone would have lit it.

**What it leaves:** two pairs under AND, and both are consistent with every test.
- relegel+vepalu
- vepalu+sufilo

My last test only narrowed the choice to these two, so this answer is a 50/50 guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = relegel, vepalu
One last question. If only relegel were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No**, relegel alone would not light the machine.

The only pairs that fit all four results are relegel+vepalu and vepalu+sufilo, both under the AND rule. The machine lights only when both nexioms are on it.

- **If the pair is relegel+vepalu:** relegel alone is only one of the two nexioms, so the machine stays dark.
- **If the pair is vepalu+sufilo:** relegel is not a nexiom at all, so the machine stays dark.

The other rules don't change this:
- **OR and XOR with sufilo:** the dark result for relegel+sufilo already ruled these out.
- **XOR with relegel:** relegel+vepalu would have stayed dark on test 2, which had both of them on it. That test lit up, so this is ruled out too.

PROBE: no
